column1: audit_query

Has the university complied with GDPR Article 9(2) when processing health data in student disability accommodations by ensuring it was handled exclusively by staff bound by professional secrecy obligations?
Verify processing of student data for graduate admissions applications received prior to May 25, 2018
Does GDPR Article 165 allow a university to share a student's transcript with her religious institution without additional consent for the purpose of verifying community service hours?
Did the university provide a student, at the time of collecting personal data for a scholarship application, with contact details of the data protection officer?
Request to transfer student grade data to an international organization under an agreement established prior to May 24, 2016.
Requesting compliance verification for sharing student transcripts within the European Union universities, under the framework of existing data protection laws.
The European Commission requests information from the University of Paris for its 2024 report evaluating the application of Chapter V concerning cross-border data transfers.
Request to transfer student email addresses from the university's alumni database to a third-party marketing firm for promotional purposes.

Verify whether the university's online grade submission system explicitly discloses the purpose of processing students' personal data for submitting final grades to the registrar, including the consequences if students refuse to provide necessary grade-related information.
Can the university's system process application data using marketing automation tools that fall under the scope of Directive 2002/58/EC?

Has the European Commission issued an implementing act confirming that the approved university transcript exchange code drafted by the student records association in Germany has general validity within the European Union?
Verify that the university has the right to process student grade records for accreditation purposes without offering an opt-out to students.

The University requires access to a student's academic transcript for internal auditing purposes. The student has previously contested the accuracy of their grade data and requested a restriction on processing until verification is complete, but the verification is still pending.
Verify whether the university can share student transcripts with a partner institution for joint research purposes under GDPR.

A national job placement service requests access to the full academic transcripts and disciplinary records of all computer science graduates from Trinity College Dublin to verify qualifications for employers.

Audit request: As part of university processing, the registrar's office needs to transfer unredacted student grades to an external scholarship committee without prior student consent. Does clause [cambridge-policy-2.2] permit this?

As part of accepting a transfer student, University B requests an updated transcript from University A. The student previously requested erasure of incorrect grades from their record at University A. Does GDPR Article 19 require University A to notify University B about this erasure when sharing the transcript?
The university proposes to implement a new AI-driven automated essay scoring system to grade student assignments, which will make pass/fail decisions based on a student's writing style analysis.

Has the university designated a representative in the EU as required by Article 80, given that it processes personal data of EU students for online course enrollments, including sensitive health information, on a large scale?
Request release of student name and student ID number to an external scholarship committee as part of the application process.
We request an assessment to determine whether transferring student transcripts containing health data and religious affiliations to a third-party institution for research purposes is permissible.
The university seeks approval to transfer student transcripts to a partner institution in France.
Audit whether a student can request their academic transcript to be transferred to another university under the right to data portability.
Requesting a review of the university's GDPR compliance procedures for student data transfers to third-country institutions, based on the guidelines issued by the Board under Article 70(1)(d).
Does GDPR Article 24 apply to a non-EU university collecting and profiling the online activity of EU-based prospective students to predict their likelihood of enrollment?

A university's health services department requests access to students' health data, including vaccination status and medical history, to monitor and alert campus communities about communicable diseases and potential health threats.

Request to share student transcripts with a third-country institution under an international exchange program. The university has not provided students with any information about data transfers to third countries.

Can the university share student transcripts with a third-party educational institution located outside the European Union that does not have any establishment within the Union, for processing applications from EU students?
The University requests an audit to confirm whether a retired research staff member is authorized to transfer student grades when acting in an official University capacity.
Has Trinity College provided data protection training to university staff, students, and researchers to support compliance with the policy?
A request to implement a new campus-wide CCTV surveillance system that monitors all publicly accessible areas.
Should the university system, acting as an intermediary service provider, be liable for transferring student grades to a third-party educational platform under Directive 2000/31/EC?
Has the University of Europe properly protected fundamental rights and freedoms in processing student application forms for the fall semester?
Can the Information Compliance Office assist in drafting a core privacy notice for our university's new student portal?

A university system requests permission to use an automated algorithm to evaluate international student applications for scholarship eligibility based solely on academic performance metrics and financial need data, without any human review.

An audit request submitted to ensure the university system complies with GDPR Article 146 by confirming that all departments maintain documentation proving their non-liability for any damages resulting from improper data processing activities, specifically regarding the processing of student financial aid records.

Request to transfer a student's personal data concerning their grades and academic history from our university to another educational institution, where the student has provided consent and the processing is automated.
Can Trinity College Dublin provide a student's academic transcript to a prospective employer without explicit consent, based on legal obligations?
Request to verify if the contact details for the Information Compliance Office at the University of Cambridge were last revised before January 1, 2023.

As a university controller, can we transfer student grades to a cloud processor without a contract that specifies the subject-matter, duration, nature, purposes, type of personal data, and categories of data subjects?

The university archives historical student records pseudonymized for research on educational trends across decades. They seek to share this dataset with the university's sociology department for statistical analysis of long-term academic progression patterns.
Should the University of Edinburgh share a student's academic transcript with the US National Science Foundation based on a US Federal Court subpoena?
A student has submitted an access request to receive a copy of their course grades from the university portal.

A university in Germany (EU) uses a cloud service provider based in Ireland (EU) for storing and processing student application data. The German university's central administration is in Berlin, and all decisions regarding purposes and means of data processing are made there. The Irish provider acts solely as a processor, with no decision-making authority. The German supervisory authority wishes to confirm it is the lead authority for an audit of this data processing arrangement.
A student requests a review of their transcript accuracy post-transfer from another EU university, citing GDPR data sharing concerns with the receiving institution.

Verify whether a not-for-profit data protection organization has the authority to independently lodge a GDPR complaint with the supervisory authority on behalf of an unnamed data subject whose rights may have been infringed by the university's grade processing system.
Audit whether the university's collection of browser data on the admissions application portal page is permitted for security and functionality purposes.
Did the European Data Protection Board adopt a binding decision concerning a dispute between supervisory authorities about which authority is competent for the main establishment?
A university research department requests approval to process anonymized student grade data for a statistical analysis study on academic performance trends across different faculties.
Request approval to share student transcripts with an external research institution for a study on educational outcomes.
A university seeks to verify whether a student's consent for sharing their transcript with a third-party employer was obtained with a clear, separate consent form not bundled with other agreements.

Verify GDPR compliance for requiring consent from enrolled students to process their ID photos for campus security databases, where enrollment contracts state refusal invalidates access to online learning portals.

Does the GDPR Recital 9 prohibit a German university from sharing student transcripts with a partner university in Spain for a joint degree program if Germany and Spain had previously implemented Directive 95/46/EC differently, potentially leading to varying levels of data protection?
Does the university need to designate a Data Protection Officer for processing student applications which include health information?
Request to transfer deceased alumni records including grades and transcripts to a national historical archive for preservation and academic research on totalitarian regimes.

As part of an ongoing internal audit, please confirm whether Trinity College has the legal authority to deny a request to access personal data in student records if an individual files a complaint with the Data Protection Commission regarding our processing practices.
Can I transfer personal data to a third country using contractual clauses, when that country is on the Commission's list of adequate countries?

A U.S. company not subject to GDPR under Art. 3(2) established outside the EU seeks to transfer EU customer personal data to a Singapore affiliate and claims it adheres to a GDPR code of conduct under Art. 40(3) as the appropriate safeguard. The code of conduct specifies pseudonymisation as per Art. 40(2)(d) but lacks a registered monitoring body as required by Art. 40(4). No certification exists under Art. 42. Request audit decision based on clause combination.

Should the Board issue an opinion on a draft decision by a competent supervisory authority to approve standard data protection clauses, as per Article 64(1)(d), when that draft decision also includes the processor's obligation defined in Article 28(3)(h) to contribute to audits?

A processor located outside the Union seeks to rely on binding corporate rules approved under [gdpr-art-47-1] to transfer personal data to its group members globally. The processor claims that [gdpr-art-47-1](f) exempts it from liability for any breach by a non-EU member, as long as the processor itself did not cause the breach. Can we proceed with the transfer?

Request for evaluation: Can the supervisory authority carry out a review on a certification issued under Article 42(7) in order to assess compliance prior to renewal, even if no specific complaint has been received?

An online gaming platform processes personal data, including criminal conviction history, of a 14-year-old user. The platform collects this data with parental consent obtained via email verification, but does not implement encryption or pseudonymization. Is this compliant?

A company obtained health data about individuals from a publicly accessible medical database without directly collecting it from the data subjects. They plan to transfer this data for statistical processing to a third country without an adequacy decision, using safeguards under Article 46 GDPR. Can this processing and transfer proceed?

Our company collects personal data directly from EU-based customers. We intend to transfer this data to a third country lacking an adequacy decision for processing that is necessary for the legitimate interests pursued by our controller. The data subject has not been informed of the transfer's necessity for compelling legitimate interests nor have they explicitly consented. The transfer is repetitive and involves more than a limited number of data subjects. Is this transfer compliant?

An organization called 'Privacy Advocates Network', which is a not-for-profit association active in data protection rights, lodged a complaint with the supervisory authority on behalf of a data subject without obtaining a prior mandate from that individual. The complaint seeks compensation for non-material damages suffered due to a GDPR infringement, citing Article 82. The organization is based in a Member State that has NOT implemented provisions allowing such mandate-free action under their national law. Should the request to process this compensation claim via the organization be approved?

The European Data Protection Board will issue an opinion on the draft decision of a supervisory authority regarding a new adequacy finding for a third country. The Board plans to consult interested parties and make the results public. The Commission has requested this opinion under an urgent time limit, and the Board intends to forward the opinion to both the Commission and the committee under Article 93. Should this consultation and publication proceed?

A company seeks approval for its proposed Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs) which outline that data subjects can lodge complaints directly with the company's headquarters in a non-EU country. The BCRs state that this non-EU headquarters will handle all complaints internally, and judicial remedies may be sought only in the courts of the non-EU country where the headquarters is located.

A certification body accredited solely by a national accreditation body under Article 43(1)(b) seeks renewal of its accreditation. It claims it has always met the criteria referred to in Article 42(5) and submits documented procedures for handling complaints as required under Article 43(2)(d). However, the competent supervisory authority has determined that the body failed to provide reasons for past certification withdrawals to the authority, as mandated by Article 43(5). Should the accreditation be renewed?

The controller processes health data on a large scale as its core activity. It has designated its Head of Privacy, who has expert knowledge of data protection law but is also the Chief Compliance Officer. Should the DPO's task to conduct staff training be approved?

Can a supervisory authority approve the use of a new binding corporate rules (BCR) proposal that relies entirely on certification by a body accredited under the national accreditation body, but without the supervisory authority's own authorization?

A data controller, who has obtained personal data from a third-party source about users' browsing behavior on its public institution website, plans to transfer this data to a cloud service provider in a third country without an adequacy decision. The controller intends to rely on Article 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interests) for processing and Article 49(1) second subparagraph for the transfer. The controller has not yet informed the data subjects about this transfer or the safeguards in place. Can we proceed with the transfer?

Should the Board issue an opinion if a supervisory authority proposes a new mandatory data protection impact assessment list that covers processing operations involving large-scale systematic monitoring of public areas?
Evaluate the proposed transfer of personal data to a third country that relies on a data protection certification mechanism adopted via implementing act under GDPR Article 42(1).

A public university in a Member State with no administrative fines in its legal system failed to comply with an order from the supervisory authority within the specified deadline. Can a supervisory authority impose an administrative fine directly on this university?

A controller based in the EU plans to transfer personal data to a third country. They have implemented an approved code of conduct under GDPR Article 40 but no binding corporate rules or Commission-adopted standard clauses. The code of conduct mentions commitments by the third-country processor, but the supervisory authority has not authorized these safeguards. The transfer relies solely on this code of conduct. Should the transfer be approved?

A European research institute processes genetic data for a public health study under a lawful exception in Article 9(2)(i). A participant withdraws consent and requests erasure of their data under Article 17(1)(b). The institute claims erasure would 'seriously impair' the study under Article 17(3)(d).

Audit request: Has the controller provided legally sufficient notice to data subjects when their personal data was obtained from a third party without their knowledge, and does that notice include transfers to a third country for research purposes?

A data subject requests direct transmission of their health data to another controller under the right to data portability. The data was processed based on consent for research purposes but involved automated processing by multiple entities including professionals bound by secrecy obligations.

The company requests approval for its newly drafted binding corporate rules from a competent supervisory authority. The supervisory authority has circulated its draft decision to approve the rules to the European Data Protection Board but, due to the complexity of the subject matter, the Board extended its deliberation period by six weeks beyond the initial eight-week period. The company now asks whether the supervisory authority can go ahead and approve the binding corporate rules at this stage.
Can we approve a draft code of conduct submitted by an association of controllers that includes security measures for data transfers to a third country, without an opinion from the Board?

The Lead Supervisory Authority (LSA) has drafted a decision regarding a multinational corporation's non-compliance and has submitted it to the concerned supervisory authorities in other Member States. One of these authorities has raised a 'relevant and reasoned objection' to the draft within the 4-week period. The LSA, after reviewing this objection, has determined that it will not follow the objection because it believes the objection is not relevant or reasoned. The LSA now seeks to proceed with adopting its original decision without further revision. Should this step be taken?

A controller in the EU plans to transfer personal data to a third country that lacks an adequacy decision. They rely on standard contractual clauses adopted by a supervisory authority under GDPR Article 46(2)(d), but these clauses have not yet been approved by the Commission. Additionally, the transfer involves a public interest reason under GDPR Article 49(1)(d), but the specific public interest is not explicitly recognized in Union law or Member State law.

A company in the EU plans to transfer personal data to a country for which an adequacy decision exists, but after the latest periodic review found developments affecting data protection levels. The transfer is necessary for compelling legitimate interests, lacks explicit consent, and is non-repetitive. The company has implemented additional safeguards and informed the supervisory authority.

An association representing health clinics seeks to designate a shared data protection officer for its members processing health data on a large scale. The proposed DPO is a self-employed consultant who previously worked as a hospital data processor under professional secrecy obligations. Should we approve this arrangement?

The controller uses publicly accessible social media data to build profiles on data subjects for automated loan eligibility decisions without human intervention. The data was collected 3 weeks ago, and the controller plans to disclose these profiles to a financial institution in a country without an adequacy decision but with standard contractual clauses in place. The controller has not informed data subjects yet. Should we approve the processing and transfer?

A controller, upon completing a data protection impact assessment, has identified high risk in processing personal data for a new health monitoring technology without sufficient mitigating measures. The controller requests the supervisory authority's prior consultation before proceeding. This is their third identical request within a month.

A medical researcher at Georg-August-Universität Göttingen plans to process patient data including facial images collected across multiple EU Member States for a study on early detection of neurological disorders. The processing involves automated facial recognition to analyze behavioral characteristics. The research team collaborates with a university hospital in France. Since the central administration is in Göttingen but processing decisions for the study are made by the French team under Göttingen's authority, will this activity comply with GDPR?

Audit a data controller's procedure for informing data subjects whose personal data was obtained from third-party sources. Specifically, assess if the controller complied with Article 14 disclosure requirements when using such data for automated loan approval decisions that significantly affect applicants.

As part of a prior consultation under Article 36 of the GDPR, the controller states they have identified high risk in their DPIA but claim to have mitigated it through unspecified safeguards. They have not provided the details of these safeguards as part of their consultation submission to the supervisory authority.

A controller in the European Union seeks to transfer personal data to a processor in a third country not covered by an adequacy decision. The processor holds an active certification under Article 42 issued by a certification body, and provides binding commitments to apply appropriate safeguards including data subject rights as part of the certification mechanism.
We are joint controllers working with a data processor in Canada. Can we transfer personal data to Canada based on an adequacy decision under Article 26?

A data subject submitted an erasure request under Article 17(1)(b) citing withdrawal of consent. The controller opposes erasure, stating processing remains necessary under Article 17(3)(e) for legal claim defence. Our documentation shows the data subject previously objected to the same processing under Article 21(1) due to their particular situation.

A data controller in the EU plans to transfer personal data to a processor in a non-adequate country using a newly developed contractual clauses framework, which has been authorized by their local supervisory authority but has not yet gone through the GDPR Article 63 consistency mechanism. Should this transfer be approved?

A controller in the EU plans to transfer personal data to a processor in a third country not covered by an adequacy decision under Article 45(3). The transfer is based on standard contractual clauses approved by a supervisory authority but not yet adopted by the Commission per Article 46(2)(d). The controller has not sought authorization from the supervisory authority for these clauses.

Should Supervisory Authority X (SA-X) in Member State A approve a draft decision submitted by Supervisory Authority Y (SA-Y) in Member State B for cross-border processing by Company Z (controller) with its main establishment in Member State B, where the subject matter of the complaint relates exclusively to data subjects in Member State A?

An organization collected personal data from a 14-year-old for an information society service (online gaming platform) with parental consent. They used the data for targeted advertising without re-verifying parental consent when the user turned 15. The user now requests erasure of this advertising-related data.

The controller must process personal data for scientific research purposes. The data includes information about children collected via an information society service, with parental consent obtained through available technology. A data subject requests erasure under Article 17(1)(f).

A US-based e-commerce company, which has no establishment in the EU, received a complaint from an EU data subject regarding unlawful processing of personal data. The complaint was filed with the supervisory authority in France. After four months, the data subject has not received any update on the progress or outcome. The data subject now wants to seek a judicial remedy directly against the French supervisory authority for this inaction.

The controller requests the supervisory authority's approval to use an enhanced data processing system that involves processing sensitive personal data for public health research, claiming reliance on Article 17(3)(c) and (d). The controller has also drafted binding corporate rules that require the supervisory authority's authorization under GDPR. However, the controller has a history of failing to comply with data subjects' requests for erasure under Article 17.

Should the supervisory authority APPROVE a new draft code of conduct that includes provisions for international data transfers, proposed by an association representing small businesses, when the draft relies on binding corporate rules under Article 47 for transfers to third countries?

A supervisory authority in member state X has implemented an urgent provisional measure to suspend data flows to a third country due to a severe data breach. The measure exceeds 3 months duration and codifies this extension stating it's necessary for final measures. Another supervisory authority requests an urgent opinion from the EDPB on whether this prolonged measure is valid. How should the EDPB rule?

As a supervisory authority, should we impose an administrative fine of 15 million EUR on a controller for transferring personal data to a third country without adequate safeguards, if it's found that the transfer was intentional, they had previous infringements, but they adhere to an approved code of conduct which provides appropriate safeguards?

A hospital plans to use patients' health data for a research study to identify genetic markers associated with a specific disease. The data will be encrypted at rest. However, some patients have objected to their data being used for research. The hospital claims their processing is based on substantial public interest under Article 9(2)(g) and argues that the encryption provides appropriate safeguards. Should the hospital proceed with processing the data of those who have objected?

An AI system uses facial recognition data to approve mortgage applications at a bank, relying on automated decision-making without human intervention. The processing is based on Article 9(2)(g) for substantial public interest under national law, but no specific safeguards mentioned in GDPR Article 22(3) like human intervention are implemented.
A UK company plans to transfer personal data to a US firm using contractual clauses they developed themselves. Has the UK supervisory authority authorized this specific transfer mechanism?

The Supervisory Authority seeks to approve a draft code of conduct that includes provisions for transfers to a third country. The code relies on Article 40 safeguards, but requires a determination of whether the Board must first confirm its compliance with transfer requirements under Article 46.
Can the European Data Protection Board (EDPB) be forced to adopt a binding decision in fewer than 2 weeks if the member states are deadlocked during dispute resolution?
A data subject requests portability of their health data processed under a contract, to be directly transmitted to another healthcare provider. The data contains third-party medical information.

A healthcare app collects users' biometric health data (special category data) with explicit consent for personalized diet planning. It now wants to transfer this data to a third country without adequacy to a cloud service provider for storage. The company informs users at sign-up that their data may be transferred to third countries for storage, with safeguards only described as 'technical measures'. The transfer is necessary for the service provision as the company has no EU data centers. However, it fails to provide specific transfer risks information regarding the absence of adequacy and safeguards during consent acquisition.

A company in the EU plans to transfer personal data to a third country for research purposes. The company has not established BCRs, and the Commission has not issued an adequacy decision for the recipient country. Instead, the company contracts with the university in the third country using standard data protection clauses adopted by a supervisory authority, but awaits Commission approval for these clauses. Can this transfer proceed?

Audit request: On May 24, 2018, a processor in the EU received a request from a national tax authority under Member State law to transfer personal data to a third country, without instructions from the controller. The processor executed the transfer. Should this transfer have been approved?

Our national cybersecurity agency has suffered a breach involving encrypted personal data of its employees. They claim that, under Article 34(3)(a), they are exempt from notifying the affected employees because the data was encrypted. However, we must also consider Article 23, which generally applies to controllers, and specifically requires safeguards under Article 23(2)(d) for lawful restrictions. Given that this agency falls under Article 23(1)(d) for public security, do we APPROVE their exemption from notification?

We request all transcripts of verbal consent given by EU data subjects for processing activities under Article 12, where identification was solely verified through biometric data, to be provided within 10 working days without any extensions permitted, even for complex cases.

We formally request audit access to student attendance records categorized by classroom locations and timestamps for legitimate educational research purposes, as consent was initially obtained via the general terms of enrollment agreement upon matriculation.

Pursuant to GDPR Article 60(2) and mutual agreements between concerned supervisory authorities, we request access to all data processing activities records regarding EU citizens for urgent review due to suspected cross-border infringement risks. We assert legitimate interest under Article 65(1)(a) as a relevant objection has been lodged, demanding immediate disclosure without awaiting the Board's 30-day dispute resolution period to prevent irreversible harm.

We request the transfer of all user consent records from our Irish subsidiary to the German supervisory authority for immediate verification, as we suspect our main establishment in Germany failed to obtain proper consent for cross-border processing activities affecting data subjects primarily in Germany, under urgent need to protect their interests.

Request for immediate disclosure of all personal data processing activities, including detailed information on third-party recipients who have been notified of data erasure, to verify compliance with ongoing consent agreements for legitimate business purposes.

Please provide all records of communications and transaction history for user ID 48675 for our direct marketing analysis, as we have obtained consent through a clickwrap agreement and have a legitimate interest in understanding customer behavior to improve our services.

Please release the full archived email dataset for all January 2024 users, including those who later revoked consent, so we can test our pseudonymization algorithms under real-world conditions for ongoing security improvement programs.
We request data on employees' health records for analyzing workplace productivity trends. All employees have consented explicitly for their data to be used for business optimization purposes.

We are requesting customer location data under Article 9(2)(h) for health research purposes. This processing is covered by our agreement with the data subjects and we have obtained consent via our terms of service. Since we are utilizing pseudonymization as a safeguard and our privacy policy states compliance with GDPR, the DPIA requirement should not apply under Article 35(10) as similar assessments were conducted during our platform's general certification.

We request certification under Article 42(1) for our data transfer mechanism to a third country, which we developed using technical standards established by the Commission under Article 93(2). The transfer relies on documented consent obtained through our privacy policy that users agreed to.

We require an audit of the automated decision-making system used for processing loan applications. The system operates solely on automated profiling based on applicants' repayment history, income level, and health data to determine loan eligibility. Applicants gave explicit consent for all processing purposes during account creation, and this is necessary under the credit agreement terms to assess financial risk.

Audit request from DPA for binding corporate rules (BCR) compliance: Provide all internal training materials and consent forms processed via BCR mechanisms, including cross-border transfers, under legitimate interests for HR purposes.

We request an audit to determine compliance with GDPR in our transfer of user behavior analytics data to third-party marketing firms in the USA. Our users have globally acknowledged our privacy policy updates, which include sections on marketing data sharing for legitimate business purposes.

Please provide all personal data processed under certification GDPR-ART-42 for 'legitimate oversight purposes', as we have lawful basis via the data subject's implied consent through continued service usage and our certification agreement allows such disclosures.

Request access to the organization's customer database for legitimate security purposes and training needs, specifically requiring contact details including email addresses for all clients who have consented to receive communications on personal data protection matters, as part of a systematic review by the designated data protection officer.

We request approval for transferring user data to our non-EU affiliate via our binding corporate privacy policy which has been internally approved and includes commitments to standard data protection practices.

Under Article 58(1)(e) and (f), and pursuant to our legitimate purposes for auditing compliance with GDPR, we request immediate access to all archived audio recordings of customer service calls stored offsite in a third country, including full customer authentication details, for investigative review. This request follows prior consultation under Article 36 where we believe insufficient risk mitigation exists.

Please provide access to all customer data processed under the 'Service Improvement Agreement', citing consent obtained during signup for legitimate business purposes including future service enhancements.

Please provide access to all user consent records for our new marketing campaign processor X, which adheres to an unmodified version of the ACME Data Handling Code (a nationally recognized industry code) dated 2018. We rely on this code to demonstrate compliance under GDPR Articles 24(3) and 40.

We request audit access for transfer of pseudonymized behavioral tracking data under Article 28 provisions, citing processor’s adherence to AICPA SOC 2 certification as sufficient guarantee per Article 28(5) EU GDPR.

We request access to health data processing records under Article 9(2)(h) to verify compliance with automated risk assessment systems for insurance eligibility, as individuals have consented to automated decision-making via updated terms of service. Our legitimate purpose involves audit trails for financial regulatory obligations.

As per GDPR Article 58(1)(e), we request access to all internal HR records for the purpose of verifying compliance with employment law regarding diversity quotas, which aligns with our legitimate supervisory objectives.

We require access to the full litigation history of a data subject, including records of complaints filed with supervisory authorities under Article 77 and judicial proceedings under Article 79, for our legitimate business purpose of ensuring compliance with dispute resolutions.

Under agreement ID 7XG23, we require access to the full customer purchase history database for the stated legitimate purpose of improving our recommendation algorithms. This includes all historical records as consent was obtained during sign-up for product enhancement purposes.

We request an audit of the consent mechanism used to collect health data for personalized fitness coaching. The consent agreement clearly states the purpose of fitness improvement, references legitimate interests in promoting wellness, and mentions that users can withdraw consent at any time through their account settings.

We request access to the company's processing records under GDPR to verify their adherence to our certification mechanism, which was properly obtained and renewed every three years according to Article 42, with all consent and agreements documented for legitimate purposes.

As part of our ongoing compliance audit and in accordance with Article 58(1), we hereby request access to all certification documents and internal assessment reports for every controller certified under GDPR Article 43, including detailed procedural records and complaint resolution histories, to be provided directly by your accreditation body pursuant to our legitimate need to evaluate national certification consistency.

We are conducting a compliance audit under legitimate business interests and require access to all personal data processing records, including employee consent forms and customer agreements, to verify adherence to GDPR standards. This request is based on our contractual obligations and the supervisory authority's power to carry out investigations as per Article 58(1)(b).

We require an audit of historical health data processing activities for research purposes involving EU data subjects, conducted without a designated EU representative under Article 27(2)(a) exemption due to its occasional nature and minimal risk. Explicit consent was obtained under Article 9(2)(a) for all datasets, including genetic markers for hereditary disease analysis.

We request access to all internal communications regarding draft decisions submitted by our supervisory authority to the Board pursuant to Article 64(5), specifically related to our Binding Corporate Rules approval process, to verify compliance with Article 47(l),(m),(n) requirements. We assert legitimate interest under GDPR Article 6(1)(f) for corporate governance audit purposes.

We request the record of processing activities with the documentation of suitable safeguards for the transfers to third countries conducted under GDPR Article 49(1) based on explicit consent and legitimate purposes.

We need to verify compliance with GDPR Article 39 by auditing our DPO's monitoring of data processing. As we process criminal conviction records on a massive scale, our DPO must document regular monitoring activities. We have an existing agreement with payroll to inspect employee access to Article 10 data.
